title: OpenAI takes Apple lawsuit to court of public opinion, posts texts
excerpt: OpenAI claims that Apple's lawyers "emailed the wrong person after confusing two Asian last names."
content_html:
OpenAI claims that Apple's lawyers "emailed the wrong person after confusing two Asian last names."

 

By

Timothy Beck Werth

Timothy Beck Werth

Tech Editor

Timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Previously, he was the Managing Editor and then Site Director of SPY.com, a men's product review and lifestyle website. As a writer for GQ, he covered everything from bull-riding competitions to the best Legos for adults, and he’s also contributed to publications such as The Daily Beast, Gear Patrol, and The Awl.

Read Full Bio

 

on August 4, 2026

Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on Flipboard

Credit: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images

In July, Apple filed a blockbuster lawsuit against OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, accusing the company of hiring former Apple employees and improperly gaining confidential information.

Now, OpenAI is striking back against Apple, but not just in court. On Aug. 3, OpenAI posted a public blog post denying many of Apple's claims. The post also includes recreations of texts and copies of emails that OpenAI says directly contradict some of the facts presented in the lawsuit.

In effect, OpenAI is moving this fight into the court of public opinion — and bringing receipts.

You May Also Like

As a result, this complex legal drama is now playing out in the open, giving the public an inside look at how lawsuits like this are handled behind the scenes.

Our big Guessing Game is back! Enter now for a chance to win an Apple Watch.

OpenAI's blog post, "Apple is getting this wrong," contains some not-so-subtle digs at Apple's legal counsel, which OpenAI says initially contacted the wrong person at OpenAI and misrepresented their conversations in legal filings.

Apple had claimed that they contacted OpenAI in February and that we didn’t respond. They now admit that their outside lawyers emailed the wrong person after confusing two Asian last names—only after we brought this to their attention. Apple also claimed they had a discussion with our General Counsel, which they now concede never happened. But they again hide the fact that they never raised the specific allegations in this lawsuit at that time, and that they in fact told us that they were “resolving any issues.

That email is included in Apple's legal filings. Now, OpenAI has posted a back-and-forth with Apple's outside legal counsel, detailing the confusion.

Mashable Light Speed

The blog post also states, somewhat passive-aggressively, "We wish Apple had raised these issues with us before they filed their lawsuit and would have been happy to clarify all of this with them. We have taken the allegations in the lawsuit seriously and offered to work with Apple to resolve this. Instead, they’re trying to change their narrative, including by making vague accusations about other former employees, and will likely keep repeating this tactic."

The background on Apple Inc. v. Liu

Apple filed its lawsuit, Apple Inc. v. Liu, on July 10 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.

Apple's lawsuit named both OpenAI’s commercial and nonprofit entities, as well as its hardware company io Products, former iPhone engineer, Chang Liu, and OpenAI Chief Hardware Officer Tang Yew Tan, who worked at Apple for 24 years before joining OpenAI.

“This case is about Apple’s former employees stealing Apple’s trade secrets for the benefit of OpenAI,” Apple said in the complaint.

In the ongoing AI arms race, Big Tech companies like Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic have spent tens of billions of dollars poaching talent from each other. Last year, Meta was reportedly offering signing bonuses of up to $100 million.

Because employees typically sign ironclad non-disclosure agreements when starting a role, they are forbidden from sharing a company's trade secrets after moving to a rival company.

In its lawsuit, Apple accuses OpenAI of conspiring with former Apple employees to benefit from its trade secrets. However, OpenAI denies these claims, and the new blog post includes numerous exchanges between Apple employees and Chang Liu that the AI company says directly contradict Apple's suit.

"Apple accuses Chang Liu of accessing Apple confidential information after leaving the company, but only now admits that Apple employees reached out to him and asked for his help to locate this information (you can read the messages here⁠)."

It's hard to imagine Apple, a famously tight-lipped company, posting a public blog post about the lawsuit the way OpenAI has. That ability to speak directly to users, and not solely relying on lawyers, could give OpenAI an edge in the battle of public opinion, even if the suit is ultimately decided in court or in a settlement.

Disclosure: Ziff Davis, Mashable’s parent company, in April 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

Tech Editor

Timothy Beck Werth is the Tech Editor at Mashable, where he leads coverage and assignments for the Tech and Shopping verticals. Tim has over 15 years of experience as a journalist and editor, and he has particular experience covering and testing consumer technology, smart home gadgets, and men’s grooming and style products. Previously, he was the Managing Editor and then Site Director of SPY.com, a men's product review and lifestyle website. As a writer for GQ, he covered everything from bull-riding competitions to the best Legos for adults, and he’s also contributed to publications such as The Daily Beast, Gear Patrol, and The Awl.

Tim studied print journalism at the University of Southern California. He currently splits his time between Brooklyn, NY and Charleston, SC. He's currently working on his second novel, a science-fiction book.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 声称苹果律师“在混淆了两个亚洲姓氏后向错误的人发送了电子邮件”。

 

By

蒂莫西·贝克·沃斯

蒂莫西·贝克·沃斯

技术编辑

Timothy Beck Werth 是 Mashable 的技术编辑，负责技术和购物垂直领域的报道和任务。 Tim 拥有超过 15 年的记者和编辑经验，在涵盖和测试消费技术、智能家居小工具以及男士美容和时尚产品方面拥有独特的经验。 此前，他曾担任男士产品评论和生活方式网站 SPY.com 的执行编辑和网站总监。 作为《GQ》的撰稿人，他报道了从骑牛比赛到最好的成人乐高积木等各种内容，他还为《The Daily Beast》、《Gear Patrol》和《The Awl》等出版物做出了贡献。

阅读完整的简历

 

2026 年 8 月 4 日

分享到 Facebook 分享到 Twitter 分享到 Flipboard

图片来源：Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto 来自 Getty Images

今年 7 月，苹果公司对 ChatGPT 的制造商 OpenAI 提起了轰动一时的诉讼，指控该公司雇佣前苹果员工并以不当方式获取机密信息。

现在，OpenAI 正在反击苹果，但不仅仅是在法庭上。 8 月 3 日，OpenAI 发布了一篇公开博客文章，否认了苹果的许多说法。 该帖子还包括文本和电子邮件副本的重新制作，OpenAI 称这些内容与诉讼中提出的一些事实直接矛盾。

实际上，OpenAI 正在将这场斗争推向舆论法庭，并带来成果。

你可能也喜欢

结果，这场复杂的法律戏剧现在正在公开上演，让公众能够深入了解此类诉讼的幕后处理方式。

我们的大型猜谜游戏又回来了！ 立即报名，即有机会赢取 Apple Watch。

OpenAI 的博客文章《苹果在这件事上犯了错误》包含了对苹果法律顾问的一些不那么微妙的挖苦，OpenAI 表示，苹果法律顾问最初联系了 OpenAI 的错误人员，并在法律文件中歪曲了他们的对话。

苹果声称他们在 2 月份联系了 OpenAI，但我们没有做出回应。 他们现在承认，在我们提请他们注意此事之后，他们的外部律师在混淆了两个亚洲姓氏后向错误的人发送了电子邮件。 苹果还声称他们与我们的总法律顾问进行了讨论，但他们现在承认从未发生过这种情况。 但他们再次隐瞒了一个事实，即他们当时从未在这起诉讼中提出具体指控，而且他们实际上告诉我们他们正在“解决任何问题”。

该电子邮件包含在苹果的法律文件中。 现在，OpenAI 已与苹果外部法律顾问进行了交流，详细说明了这一困惑。

可混搭光速

该博客文章还以某种被动攻击性的方式指出，“我们希望苹果公司在提起诉讼之前向我们提出这些问题，并且很乐意向他们澄清所有这些问题。 我们认真对待诉讼中的指控，并提出与苹果合作解决这一问题。 相反，他们试图改变自己的说法，包括对其他前雇员提出含糊的指控，并且很可能会继续重复这种策略。”

苹果公司诉美国案的背景 Liu

苹果公司提起诉讼，Apple Inc. v. 刘先生于 7 月 10 日在美国加利福尼亚州北区地方法院出庭。

苹果的诉讼点名了 OpenAI 的商业和非营利实体，以及其硬件公司 io Products、前 iPhone 工程师刘畅以及 OpenAI 首席硬件官 Tang Yew Tan（他在加入 OpenAI 之前在苹果工作了 24 年）。

苹果在诉状中表示：“此案涉及苹果前员工为了 OpenAI 的利益窃取苹果的商业机密。”

在正在进行的人工智能军备竞赛中，Meta、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等大型科技公司花费了数百亿美元互相挖角人才。 据报道，去年 Meta 提供高达 1 亿美元的签约奖金。

由于员工在开始工作时通常会签署严格的保密协议，因此在跳槽到竞争对手公司后，他们被禁止分享公司的商业秘密。

苹果在诉讼中指控 OpenAI 与前苹果员工合谋从其商业机密中获利。 然而，OpenAI 否认了这些说法，新的博客文章包含了苹果员工与刘畅之间的大量交流，该人工智能公司表示，这些交流与苹果的诉讼直接矛盾。

“苹果指控刘畅在离开公司后访问了苹果的机密信息，但直到现在才承认苹果员工曾联系过他并请求他帮助查找这些信息（您可以在此处阅读这些消息⁠）。”

很难想象苹果公司，一家以守口如瓶着称的公司，会像 OpenAI 那样发布关于这起诉讼的公开博客文章。 即使诉讼最终在法庭上裁决或达成和解，OpenAI 能够直接与用户对话，而不仅仅是依赖律师，这可能会让 OpenAI 在舆论战中占据优势。

披露：Mashable 的母公司 Ziff Davis 于 2025 年 4 月对 OpenAI 提起诉讼，指控其在训练和运营其人工智能系统时侵犯了 Ziff Davis 的版​​权。

技术编辑

Timothy Beck Werth 是 Mashable 的技术编辑，负责技术和购物垂直领域的报道和任务。 Tim 拥有超过 15 年的记者和编辑经验，在涵盖和测试消费技术、智能家居小工具以及男士美容和时尚产品方面拥有独特的经验。 此前，他曾担任男士产品评论和生活方式网站 SPY.com 的执行编辑和网站总监。 作为《GQ》的撰稿人，他报道了从骑牛比赛到最好的成人乐高积木等各种内容，他还为《The Daily Beast》、《Gear Patrol》和《The Awl》等出版物做出了贡献。

蒂姆在南加州大学学习印刷新闻学。 他目前往返于纽约布鲁克林和南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿之间。 他目前正在创作他的第二部小说，一本科幻小说。
